name: SIP Calculator
short: Future value of a monthly SIP
description: Work out what a monthly systematic investment plan could grow to, and compare it with putting the same total in as a lump sum.

faqs.q: How does this SIP calculator work out the maturity value?
faqs.a: It treats each instalment as invested at the start of the month and compounds it monthly at one-twelfth of the annual return you enter. The result is the future value of an annuity due: P × [((1 + i)^n − 1) ÷ i] × (1 + i).

faqs.q: Are mutual fund SIP returns guaranteed?
faqs.a: No. Equity and hybrid fund returns move with the market. The expected return you enter is an assumption, not a promise, and actual NAV-based returns can be higher or lower in any year.

faqs.q: Is a 12% expected return realistic?
faqs.a: It depends on the fund category and the period. Use a lower figure for debt and hybrid funds, and test a range of returns for equity funds rather than relying on a single number.

faqs.q: Does the calculator account for tax and exit load?
faqs.a: No. Capital gains tax, exit loads and expense ratios are not deducted. Fund NAVs already reflect the expense ratio, but tax on redemption is payable separately.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss an SIP instalment?
faqs.a: Most fund houses simply skip the missed instalment. Several consecutive misses can lead to the SIP being cancelled, but units already bought stay invested.

name: Lumpsum Calculator
description: See how a single investment compounds over time at an assumed annual return, and how it compares with spreading the same amount through an SIP.

faqs.q: What formula does the lumpsum calculator use?
faqs.a: Future value = P × (1 + r)^t, where P is the amount invested, r is the expected annual return and t is the number of years. Returns are compounded once a year.

faqs.q: Is lumpsum better than SIP?
faqs.a: If markets rise steadily, a lumpsum invested early usually ends higher because the whole amount compounds for longer. An SIP spreads the entry price across market levels, which reduces the risk of investing everything at a peak.

faqs.q: Can I use this for fixed deposits?
faqs.a: Only approximately. Bank FDs usually compound quarterly, so use the FD calculator for deposit maturity values.

faqs.q: Does inflation reduce the value shown?
faqs.a: The figure shown is in future rupees. To see its value in today's money, divide it by (1 + inflation)^years.

faqs.q: Are returns on lumpsum mutual fund investments taxed?
faqs.a: Yes. Gains are taxed as capital gains when you redeem units. The rate depends on the fund type and how long you held the units.

name: Step-up SIP Calculator
description: Model an SIP that increases by a fixed percentage every year, in line with salary hikes, and see the gap it opens over a flat SIP.

faqs.q: What is a step-up SIP?
faqs.a: A step-up or top-up SIP raises the monthly instalment by a set percentage or amount once a year. Most fund houses let you set this when you register the SIP.

faqs.q: How is the step-up applied in this calculator?
faqs.a: The instalment stays the same for 12 months, then rises by the step-up percentage. Each instalment is invested at the start of the month and compounded monthly.

faqs.q: How much step-up is sensible?
faqs.a: Many investors match it to their expected annual salary increase, often 5% to 10%. A step-up that outpaces income growth may be hard to sustain.

faqs.q: Can I stop the step-up later?
faqs.a: Yes. You can usually modify or cancel the top-up through the fund house or your platform, while keeping the base SIP running.

faqs.q: Why does the step-up make such a large difference?
faqs.a: Later instalments are larger, and every year's higher amount then compounds for the rest of the term, so the effect builds over long periods.

name: SWP Calculator
description: Plan a systematic withdrawal plan: how much you can take out each month, what is left at the end, and when the money runs out at a given return.

faqs.q: How does an SWP work?
faqs.a: You invest a lump sum in a mutual fund and instruct the fund house to redeem a fixed amount every month. The remaining units stay invested and continue to earn returns.

faqs.q: How is the balance worked out each month?
faqs.a: The balance earns one month of return, then the withdrawal is taken out: B(next) = B × (1 + i) − W, where i is the monthly return.

faqs.q: What happens if withdrawals exceed returns?
faqs.a: The corpus shrinks every month. The calculator shows the month in which it would run out at the return you assume.

faqs.q: How are SWP withdrawals taxed?
faqs.a: Each withdrawal is a redemption of units, so only the gain portion is taxed as capital gains, not the full amount withdrawn.

faqs.q: Is a fixed monthly withdrawal safe in a falling market?
faqs.a: Withdrawing a fixed amount when NAVs are low sells more units, which can deplete the corpus faster. Many investors keep one to two years of withdrawals in a debt fund to manage this.

name: PPF Calculator
description: Calculate the maturity value of yearly Public Provident Fund deposits over the 15-year term and any five-year extensions.

faqs.q: What is the current PPF interest rate?
faqs.a: TradeTarget's PPF guide puts the rate at 7.1% a year, compounded annually. The government reviews it every quarter, so check the latest notification before you invest.

faqs.q: How much can I deposit in PPF?
faqs.a: At least ₹500 and at most ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year, in one go or in instalments.

faqs.q: How does this calculator treat deposits?
faqs.a: It assumes the full yearly deposit is made at the start of the year, before 5 April, so it earns interest for the whole year.

faqs.q: Can I extend a PPF account after 15 years?
faqs.a: Yes, in blocks of five years, with or without fresh deposits. Use the tenure slider to model 20, 25 or 30 years.

faqs.q: Is PPF interest taxable?
faqs.a: No. Deposits qualify for deduction under Section 80C in the old regime, and interest and maturity proceeds are tax-free.

name: EPF Calculator
description: Estimate your Employees' Provident Fund balance at retirement from your basic pay, annual increments and the EPF interest rate.

faqs.q: How much goes into EPF every month?
faqs.a: You contribute 12% of basic pay plus dearness allowance. Your employer also contributes 12%, of which up to 8.33% (capped at ₹1,250 a month) goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme and the rest to EPF.

faqs.q: What interest rate does the calculator use?
faqs.a: It defaults to 8.25%, the rate in TradeTarget's EPF guide. EPFO declares the rate every financial year.

faqs.q: How is EPF interest calculated?
faqs.a: Interest is worked out monthly on the running balance at one-twelfth of the annual rate and credited to the account once a year.

faqs.q: Does the result include my pension?
faqs.a: No. The EPS share of the employer contribution builds a pension entitlement, not a lump sum, so it is shown separately and left out of the EPF corpus.

faqs.q: Is the EPF corpus tax-free?
faqs.a: Withdrawals after five years of continuous service are tax-free. Interest on employee contributions above ₹2.5 lakh a year is taxable.

name: FD Calculator
description: Find the maturity value and interest earned on a fixed deposit for any tenure and compounding frequency.

faqs.q: How is FD maturity calculated?
faqs.a: Maturity = P × (1 + r/n)^(n × t), where r is the annual rate, n the number of compounding periods a year and t the tenure in years. Most banks compound quarterly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between cumulative and payout FDs?
faqs.a: A cumulative FD reinvests interest and pays everything at maturity, which is what this calculator shows. A payout FD pays interest monthly or quarterly and returns only the principal at maturity.

faqs.q: Is FD interest taxable?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate. Banks deduct TDS once interest crosses the threshold for the year.

faqs.q: Do senior citizens get a higher rate?
faqs.a: Most banks pay senior citizens an extra 0.25% to 0.50% a year. Enter that rate to see the difference.

faqs.q: Are bank FDs insured?
faqs.a: Deposits are insured by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, covering principal and interest together.

name: RD Calculator
description: Calculate what a monthly recurring deposit pays at maturity with quarterly compounding, as most Indian banks calculate it.

faqs.q: How do banks calculate RD maturity?
faqs.a: Each monthly instalment earns interest compounded quarterly for the time it stays in the account. The calculator adds up the maturity value of every instalment.

faqs.q: What is the minimum tenure for an RD?
faqs.a: Most banks offer RDs from six months to ten years, in multiples of three months.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss an instalment?
faqs.a: Banks usually charge a small penalty for a delayed instalment. Several missed instalments can lead to the account being closed early.

faqs.q: Is RD interest taxable?
faqs.a: Yes. It is taxed at your slab rate, and banks deduct TDS once interest crosses the threshold for the year.

faqs.q: RD or SIP: which is better?
faqs.a: An RD gives a fixed, known return and suits short-term goals. An equity SIP can earn more over long periods but its value moves with the market.

name: NPS Calculator
short: Pension corpus, lump sum and annuity
description: Estimate your National Pension System corpus at 60, the lump sum you can take out, and the monthly pension from the annuity.

faqs.q: How much of the NPS corpus must buy an annuity?
faqs.a: Under the exit rules notified in December 2025, non-government subscribers must use at least 20% of the corpus to buy an annuity and can withdraw up to 80% as a lump sum. Government employees still use at least 40% for the annuity.

faqs.q: How is the monthly pension estimated?
faqs.a: Pension = annuity purchase amount × annuity rate ÷ 12. Annuity rates depend on the provider and the plan you choose.

faqs.q: What return should I assume?
faqs.a: It depends on your equity allocation. NPS lets you hold up to 75% in equity under active choice; use a lower return for a more conservative mix.

faqs.q: What tax benefits does NPS offer?
faqs.a: Under the old regime, you can claim up to ₹50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B) over and above Section 80C. Employer contributions are deductible under Section 80CCD(2) in both regimes, within limits.

faqs.q: Is the NPS lump sum taxable?
faqs.a: Up to 60% of the corpus withdrawn at exit is tax-free. The pension from the annuity is taxed as income in the year you receive it.

name: Retirement Calculator
description: Work out how large a retirement corpus you need to cover inflation-adjusted expenses, and the monthly SIP that gets you there.

faqs.q: How does the calculator estimate the corpus needed?
faqs.a: It inflates today's monthly expenses to your retirement age, then finds the amount that can fund those expenses, rising with inflation every year, until your life expectancy at the post-retirement return.

faqs.q: Why does inflation matter so much?
faqs.a: At 6% inflation, prices roughly double every 12 years. Expenses of ₹50,000 a month today would need about ₹1 lakh a month in 12 years.

faqs.q: What post-retirement return should I assume?
faqs.a: Retirees usually hold more debt, so a lower return than during working years is prudent. If the return is below inflation, the corpus needed rises sharply.

faqs.q: Are my existing savings counted?
faqs.a: Yes. Current savings are grown at the pre-retirement return and subtracted from the corpus needed before the monthly SIP is worked out.

faqs.q: Does this include EPF, PPF and NPS?
faqs.a: Add their current balances to existing savings, or use the dedicated calculators to project each one separately.

name: Home Loan EMI Calculator
description: Calculate your home loan EMI, the total interest over the tenure, and how much a prepayment saves.

faqs.q: How is a home loan EMI calculated?
faqs.a: EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly interest rate and n the number of monthly instalments.

faqs.q: How does prepayment help?
faqs.a: A prepayment reduces the outstanding principal. If you keep the EMI unchanged, the loan closes earlier and total interest falls. The calculator shows both effects.

faqs.q: Do banks charge for prepaying a floating-rate home loan?
faqs.a: RBI rules do not allow banks to charge foreclosure or prepayment penalties on floating-rate home loans taken by individuals.

faqs.q: What tax benefits are available on a home loan?
faqs.a: Under the old regime, interest up to ₹2 lakh a year on a self-occupied home is deductible under Section 24(b), and principal repayment counts towards the ₹1.5 lakh Section 80C limit.

faqs.q: Why is most of my early EMI going towards interest?
faqs.a: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which is highest at the start. As principal falls, more of each EMI goes towards repayment.

name: Car Loan EMI Calculator
description: Work out the EMI on a car loan after your down payment, and the total interest you pay over the tenure.

faqs.q: How much down payment should I make?
faqs.a: Lenders usually finance 80% to 90% of the on-road price. A larger down payment cuts the loan amount, the EMI and the total interest.

faqs.q: What tenure do car loans come in?
faqs.a: Usually one to seven years. Longer tenures lower the EMI but raise the total interest paid.

faqs.q: Is the EMI formula the same as for a home loan?
faqs.a: Yes. Car loans use the same reducing-balance EMI formula: P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1).

faqs.q: Can I prepay a car loan?
faqs.a: Most lenders allow it, but fixed-rate car loans often carry a foreclosure charge. Check your loan agreement.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include insurance and registration?
faqs.a: No. Enter the amount you plan to borrow. Insurance, registration and accessories are usually paid upfront or added to the loan separately.

name: Personal Loan EMI Calculator
description: Calculate the EMI on a personal loan, the processing fee, and the effective cost of borrowing.

faqs.q: Why are personal loan rates higher than home loan rates?
faqs.a: Personal loans are unsecured, so lenders price in more risk. Rates depend on your income, credit score and the lender.

faqs.q: How does the processing fee affect the cost?
faqs.a: The fee is deducted upfront or paid separately, so you receive less than the loan amount but repay the full amount. The calculator adds the fee to the total cost.

faqs.q: What credit score do lenders look for?
faqs.a: Most lenders prefer a score of 750 or above for the best rates. A lower score can still get a loan, usually at a higher rate.

faqs.q: Can I foreclose a personal loan?
faqs.a: Usually after a lock-in of six to twelve EMIs, with a foreclosure charge of a few per cent of the outstanding amount.

faqs.q: Is a personal loan better than a credit card balance?
faqs.a: Personal loan rates are usually well below credit card interest, so converting a large card balance into a loan can cut interest costs.

name: Income Tax Calculator
description: Compare your income tax under the old and new regimes for FY 2026-27, with deductions, rebate, surcharge and cess.

faqs.q: What are the new regime slabs for FY 2026-27?
faqs.a: Nil up to ₹4 lakh, 5% from ₹4 lakh to ₹8 lakh, 10% to ₹12 lakh, 15% to ₹16 lakh, 20% to ₹20 lakh, 25% to ₹24 lakh and 30% above ₹24 lakh. Budget 2026 left these unchanged.

faqs.q: Why is there no tax up to ₹12.75 lakh salary in the new regime?
faqs.a: Salaried taxpayers get a ₹75,000 standard deduction, and the Section 87A rebate cancels tax on taxable income up to ₹12 lakh. Marginal relief applies just above that level.

faqs.q: Which deductions are allowed under the old regime?
faqs.a: Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakh), 80D health insurance, 80CCD(1B) NPS (up to ₹50,000), home loan interest under Section 24(b) (up to ₹2 lakh), HRA exemption and a ₹50,000 standard deduction, among others.

faqs.q: Which regime should I choose?
faqs.a: Compare both with your actual deductions. The old regime usually helps only when deductions are large; the calculator shows the break-even clearly.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include surcharge and cess?
faqs.a: Yes. Surcharge applies above ₹50 lakh of income, with marginal relief, and is capped at 25% in the new regime. Health and education cess of 4% is added to tax plus surcharge.

name: HRA Calculator
description: Calculate how much of your house rent allowance is exempt from tax under Section 10(13A) for FY 2026-27.

faqs.q: How is the HRA exemption worked out?
faqs.a: The exempt amount is the lowest of three figures: the HRA you actually receive, rent paid minus 10% of basic pay plus DA, and 50% (metro) or 40% (other cities) of basic pay plus DA.

faqs.q: Which cities count as metro for HRA?
faqs.a: From FY 2026-27, the 50% limit applies to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad under the Income Tax Rules, 2026. All other cities use 40%.

faqs.q: Can I claim HRA under the new regime?
faqs.a: No. The HRA exemption is available only if you opt for the old regime.

faqs.q: Do I need my landlord's PAN?
faqs.a: Yes, if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh. Employers usually also ask for rent receipts or a rent agreement.

faqs.q: Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents?
faqs.a: Yes, if you actually pay rent and they report it as income. You cannot claim HRA for rent paid to your spouse.

name: CAGR Calculator
description: Find the compound annual growth rate between a starting and ending value, and compare it with a benchmark rate.

faqs.q: What is CAGR?
faqs.a: CAGR is the constant yearly rate at which an investment would have grown from its starting value to its ending value. It smooths out year-to-year swings.

faqs.q: How is CAGR calculated?
faqs.a: CAGR = (Ending value ÷ Beginning value)^(1 ÷ years) − 1.

faqs.q: How is CAGR different from absolute return?
faqs.a: Absolute return is the total percentage change, regardless of time. CAGR spreads that change over the number of years, so it can be compared across investments held for different periods.

faqs.q: What are the limits of CAGR?
faqs.a: It ignores volatility and assumes a single investment at the start. For SIPs or irregular cash flows, XIRR is the better measure.

faqs.q: Can CAGR be negative?
faqs.a: Yes. If the ending value is below the starting value, CAGR is negative.
